purpose: Bounded official worker-remedy record preserving court enforcement, release of funds held in trust, and reported worker-level back-pay receipt without inferring later recovery.

events.geography: Australia; Adelaide transport company and Federal Court appeal
events.date_precision: official Fair Work Ombudsman follow-up release date; underpayment occurred 2007-2009 and appeal was dismissed before the release
events.denominator: Ten named-in-the-record truck drivers; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Ombudsman enforcement follow-up record
events.missingness: Worker identities, payment instruments, household effects, later employment, trust, recurrence, health, and exit are not retained; adequacy is not assessed against each worker's losses or household needs
events.exposure: Ten truck drivers were underpaid minimum wages and other entitlements by Atkins Freight Services between 2007 and 2009
events.alternatives_before_action: The public record does not report substitute employment, bargaining alternatives, household buffers, or non-use before enforcement
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Underpayment created a reported wage and superannuation shortfall; the company appealed after a court ordered back-pay and paid funds into Court pending the appeal
events.choice_or_response: The Fair Work Ombudsman pursued legal action; the company appealed; the Federal Court dismissed the appeal and ordered release of the funds from trust
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The employer controlled original payment; the courts controlled the trust and release process; the Fair Work Ombudsman controlled the public enforcement route
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: After the appeal was dismissed, the Federal Court allowed approximately $468,000 held in trust to be released and paid to the drivers; the official record reports $374,487 in ordered back-pay plus superannuation and interest
events.remedy_receipt: The Fair Work Ombudsman reports that all ten truck drivers received back-payments ranging from $8,012 to $91,566
events.durability_followup: The public record ends at reported payment receipt; later work, household security, adequacy, trust, recurrence, health, and exit are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: Reported worker-level receipt of court-enforced back-pay after appeal funds were released
events.protected_outcome: The ordered wage, superannuation, and interest remedy reached the ten drivers according to the official follow-up
events.sacrificed_outcome: Payment was delayed through litigation and appeal; any residual loss, household strain, or lost trust is unmeasured
events.cost_risk_transfer: Workers carried the initial underpayment and delay; public enforcement and court processes transferred a payment obligation and legal risk back to the employer
events.later_outcome: The official institution reports final release and receipt of the back-payments, but no later lived-recovery endpoint
events.meaning_and_attribution: The enforcement record attributes the payment obligation to underpayment and rejects an attempt to reduce compensation through private deeds of release; it contains no worker-reported trust or meaning measure
events.public_or_collective_response: Public Fair Work Ombudsman enforcement and appellate court action are observed; no later collective or political response is reported
events.counterexample: A formal remedy can reach every worker in a small public case while leaving adequacy, trust, later livelihood, and durable recovery unobserved
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official Fair Work Ombudsman release, https://www.fairwork.gov.au/newsroom/media-releases/2018-media-releases/january-2018/20180117-atkins-appeal-dismissed; payment receipt is institutionally reported, not independently audited here

arrows.to: Fair Work Ombudsman legal action and court back-pay order
arrows.evidence: The official record reports underpayment, investigation, legal action, penalties, and a back-pay order
arrows.counterexample: A formal order does not by itself prove payment receipt
arrows.remaining_gap: Worker-level payment before the appeal process

arrows.from: appeal and funds held in trust
arrows.evidence: The official record reports that the company paid approximately $468,000 to Court pending appeal and that the Federal Court later allowed release after dismissing the appeal
arrows.counterexample: Institutional release is not identical to worker receipt
arrows.remaining_gap: Individual transfer timing and payment instrument

arrows.evidence: The official Fair Work Ombudsman release states that the drivers had received payments ranging from $8,012 to $91,566
arrows.counterexample: Reported receipt does not establish adequacy, net household effect, or restored trust
arrows.remaining_gap: Independent receipt confirmation, adequacy, household recovery, and later security

arrows.to: durable security, trust, later work, or exit
arrows.evidence: The official follow-up ends after reporting the payments
arrows.counterexample: Payment can be complete while later livelihood and trust remain unknown
arrows.remaining_gap: Later employment, household outcome, adequacy, recurrence, trust, health, and exit

boundary: This ledger closes a reported payment-receipt endpoint for ten workers in one enforcement case. It does not establish adequacy, durable recovery, prevalence, or a general enforcement success rate.
storage_boundary: No claimant file, payment instrument, or restricted data is retained; only bounded official summary fields and explicitly open downstream arrows are represented.
